clue.text: Sit back in a tree awkwardly and study

indicators.note: in says the reversed piece sits inside the jumbled letters
awkwardly suggests the letters of a and tree are arranged clumsily into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word sit from right to left

explanation.surface: Someone clambers clumsily into a tree to sit and do some reading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkwardly' makes TREAE; 'back' reverses the opening word and 'in' sets it between the fourth and fifth letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A treatise is a formal written study of a subject, a scholarly work.

clue.text: Pitch — what happens on one before match?

definitions.meaning: to pitch something is to throw or ... it

definitions.text: what happens on one before match?
definitions.meaning: before a cricket or football match the captains ... a coin on the pitch

explanation.surface: A sports question about the ritual on the field before a game begins.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition plays on 'one' meaning a pitch, so the coin toss is what happens on it before play starts.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitch and toss both mean throw; a coin toss on the field decides who starts.

clue.text: Composer who could be regal

indicators.note: could be says the letters of regal may be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: A musician whose name, or music, might seem royal.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward Elgar wrote much stately ceremonial music, such as the Pomp and Circumstance marches, so 'regal' fits the surface too.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Elgar was an English composer of the late Victorian and Edwardian era.

clue.text: Atheist hated being abused? You've got it!

indicators.note: being abused suggests the letters are maltreated and knocked out of their order

explanation.surface: An unbeliever is being insulted, and someone exclaims approvingly.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are encouraging exclamations telling someone they have understood or done the right thing.

clue.text: City boy holding a US soldier up

indicators.note: holding means one piece wraps around the other, here the boy around the rest

parts.note: a boy is a son

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the soldier's letters are read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: GI is a US soldier

explanation.surface: A lad takes an American serviceman hostage in some city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the soldier, since this is a down entry, and 'holding' wraps the boy round it. The city in Vietnam is now Ho Chi Minh City.
explanation.definitionFit: Saigon is the former name, still widely used, of Vietnam's largest metropolis.

clue.text: Incentive in some useless purchase

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A shopper is tempted into buying something pointless.
explanation.definitionFit: A spur is something that urges one on, a stimulus or motivation.

clue.text: Synthetic cobbler's model featured in illustration

indicators.note: featured in places the model inside the picture

parts.note: PIC is short for picture, an illustration
a last is the foot-shaped block a shoemaker works on

explanation.surface: A shoemaker's fake leather model appears in a drawing.
explanation.walkthrough: A cobbler is a shoe-mender; his LAST is the wooden foot-shaped form shoes are made on.
explanation.definitionFit: Plastic as an adjective means artificial, made from man-made materials.

clue.text: Modest about a bit of money (note being pocketed)

indicators.note: being pocketed says the note is tucked inside the other letters

parts.note: re means about, concerning
a cent is a small coin
ti is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone is coy about a small sum, with a banknote slipped into a pocket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being pocketed' tucks the note inside RECENT; the 'note' is musical, from do-re-mi, not a banknote.
explanation.definitionFit: A reticent person is reserved and holds back, much like a modest, unassuming one.

clue.text: A retired Eton criminal set out in a new direction

definitions.text: set out in a new direction

indicators.note: criminal suggests these letters are corrupted into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A former Eton pupil turned crook sets off on a different path in life.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton is a famous English private school.
explanation.definitionFit: To reorientate is to turn or realign towards a different course or bearing.

clue.text: Greek character's mark of disgrace, with time passing

indicators.note: passing means the time letter goes away from the word, as time passes and is gone

parts.note: a stigma is a mark of disgrace

explanation.surface: A Greek person bears a mark of shame that fades over the years.
explanation.definitionFit: Sigma is the eighteenth letter of the Greek alphabet, equivalent to S.

clue.text: Rough home with old lover getting to perform

parts.note: in means at home
an ex is a former partner
to act is to perform

explanation.surface: A rough-and-ready household where a former partner comes round to put on a show.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough estimate is an imprecise or approximate one.

clue.text: Upper-class racist actor, nasty about India

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go around the letter for India
nasty suggests the letters are spoilt and rearranged

parts.note: I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A posh, bigoted thespian is being unpleasant about India.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristocratic describes the nobility, the highest social rank.

clue.text: Support for 13 malfunctioning palmtops

definitions.note: 13 across is ALIGHT, read here as A LIGHT, which this post holds up

indicators.note: malfunctioning devices are out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Handheld computers keep breaking down and need support.
explanation.walkthrough: '13' points to the answer at 13 across, ALIGHT; read as 'a light', it is what a street post holds up.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamppost is the upright pole bearing a street lamp aloft.

clue.text: A land in flames

parts.note: to light on something is to land or settle on it

explanation.surface: A country is burning.
explanation.definitionFit: Something alight is on fire, burning.

clue.text: To trespass with intent — not half impolite!

indicators.note: not half means only one half of the word intent is kept, its first three letters

parts.note: rude means impolite

explanation.surface: Breaking in on purpose is truly bad manners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' also echoes the British exclamation meaning 'very much so!'
explanation.definitionFit: To intrude is to enter where one is not welcome, as a trespasser does.

clue.text: One minister and another holding firm

indicators.note: holding means one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: another minister is a dean, a senior cleric
CO is short for company, a firm

explanation.surface: Two clergymen run a business together.
explanation.definitionFit: A deacon is an ordained cleric ranking below a priest in many churches.

clue.text: Mad character to talk having lost head

indicators.note: having lost head means the first letter is removed

parts.note: to chatter is to talk

explanation.surface: A crazy person babbles after going out of their mind.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mad Hatter is the tea-party host in Alice's Adventures in Wonderland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hatter is Lewis Carroll's famously mad figure at the tea party.

clue.text: Pontificate wildly about king being turned to stone

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters surround the king's letter
wildly suggests the letters fly about into a new order

parts.note: R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Someone sounds off wildly about a monarch who turned to stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Petrifaction is the process of organic matter becoming fossilised rock.

clue.text: Love some style of abstractionism

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
some means a part

explanation.surface: Someone is fond of a little abstract art.
explanation.definitionFit: Op art is an abstract movement using optical illusions.

clue.text: Obvious, not the first tragic old king

indicators.note: not the first means the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: clear means obvious

explanation.surface: An old monarch, plainly not the first of his line, met a tragic end.
explanation.definitionFit: King Lear is the title figure of Shakespeare's tragedy.

clue.text: Work cut short, time to be frugal? Wealthy!

indicators.note: cut short means the last letter is lopped off

parts.note: an opus is a work, especially of music
Lent is the Christian season of fasting and self-denial

explanation.surface: Reduced working hours mean belt-tightening, yet somebody exclaims about riches.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulent means rich and luxurious, showing great affluence.

clue.text: Traffic in East Devon river heading west

indicators.note: heading west means in an across clue the letters run from right to left

parts.note: the Dart is a river in Devon

explanation.surface: Boats move along a river in east Devon, flowing westward.
explanation.walkthrough: Devon is a county in south-west England; the Dart runs through it to Dartmouth.
explanation.definitionFit: To traffic in goods is to trade or deal in them.

clue.text: Kick and pulled along, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word is identified by its sound when spoken

parts.note: towed means pulled along

explanation.surface: Something is kicked and dragged along.
explanation.definitionFit: To toe a ball is to kick it with the tip of the foot.

clue.text: Cor — heartless newspaper boss — you must give that person their due!

definitions.text: you must give that person their due!

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of the word is removed

parts.note: an editor runs a newspaper

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at a cold-hearted press chief, insisting he gets what he deserves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cor' is a British exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: A creditor is someone owed money, to whom payment is due.
